newsitem.title: USA: Cooper says explores sale of Kirsch unit.
newsitem.headline: Cooper says explores sale of Kirsch unit.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said on Monday it has engaged Morgan Stanley & Co to review strategic alternatives related to its Kirsch Division, including a possible sale of the unit.
Kirsch, a manufacturer of drapery hardware and custom window coverings, was acquired by Cooper in 1981.

In a statement, Cooper's chairman and chief executive H. John Riley said, "The window treatments industry has changed over the past several years, evolving into more of a fashion business. While Kirsch is responding to this shift by introducing many new product lines, Cooper's primary focus remains on basic, value-added manufacturing."
He added that the decision to review alternatives related to Kirsch was one of several initiatives recently taken by the company to enhance its financial position.
Kirsch had worldwide revenues of about $260 million in 1995, the company said.
